subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding and openclaw configure treat memory embedding setup as mandatory, prominently optional, or diagnostic-only, and what credential/probe UX should it use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the setup surface is missing, but the requested mandatory behavior changes first-run friction, provider dependency, credential storage, SecretRef handling, daemon environment expectations, and FTS-only/local workflows.

options.title: Prominent Optional Setup
options.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that configures provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

options.title: Mandatory Memory Gate
options.body: Require users to configure embeddings or explicitly choose FTS-only before completing onboarding, improving recall readiness at the cost of first-run friction.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep onboarding lean and rely on docs, doctor, and memory status guidance, accepting that some users may miss memory readiness until later.

recommendation.title: Prominent Optional Setup
recommendation.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that configures provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the current issue assignee and already participated in the product-scope discussion on this report.
